motivation: repair the mismatch between whole-line H1 Evans histories and wall-extended prime cut columns
finite_wall_set: A_X={0} union {log p:p<=X}, retaining both the global seam and prime cut endpoints

carrier.name: H_wall,X
carrier.definition: functions f in L2(R) whose restrictions to components of R\A_X lie in H1, with finite one-sided traces at every a in A_X
carrier.reason_complete: finite orthogonal sum of H1 interval pieces with continuous trace maps and a finite jump quadratic form

evans.jump_coordinates: all zero, including the global seam at 0

prime_cut_columns.form: c_a is piecewise H1 with its endpoint discontinuity at a retained as [c_a]_a
prime_cut_columns.membership: c_(log p) belongs to H_wall,X for p<=X
prime_cut_columns.uniform_native_norm: recovers ||Phi||_2^2+||Phi'||_2^2+|Phi(0)|^2 under the source-centered translation convention

green_identity.statement: integration by parts on each interval component produces the ordinary endpoint terms plus the finite jump pairing at A_X
green_identity.consequence: regular derivative and wall rows are one closed graph operation rather than separately normalized distributions

incidence.map: B_X:E_X->H_wall,X, e_p maps to p^(-1/2)c_(log p)
incidence.finite_reason: finite source and finite wall set
incidence.adjoint: defined uniquely by the source metric and H_wall,X graph pairing

relation_to_current_c_fp.owner_action: replace/enlarge the C_FP history domain and trace map, then recheck maximal isotropy and the block adjoint

completion_requirements: choose a countable-wall weight for jumps at log p
prove B is bounded/Hilbert-Schmidt in the resulting wall graph norm
prove local finiteness and closedness of the countable broken-domain differential
extend Fourier-Poisson sewing to wall coordinates
prove the completed Green boundary relation remains maximal isotropic
disposition: At every finite cutoff, the broken-H1 history-plus-wall graph is the explicit common domain previously missing: it contains both unchanged Evans histories and raw prime cut columns, and totalizes derivative plus wall distributions in one closed operator. Adoption by the conservative cone and countable completion remain open.
